newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Blair boosted by keynote speech -poll.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair boosted by keynote speech -poll.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair has given his Labour Party a big electoral fillip with a speech on Tuesday to its pre-election annual conference, an opinion poll indicated on Saturday.

The Gallup survey in the Daily Telegraph newspaper said Labour's ratings rose to 57 percent after the speech from 52 percent before it, while the percentage of people supporting the ruling Conservatives fell to 24 from 27.5.
Both before and after the speech, the minority Liberal Democrats stood at 15 percent.
Prime Minister John Major, who will address the annual Conservative conference next Friday, must call an election by May next year.
Gallup interviewed 1,047 electors between September 26 and October 1 for its initial survey, and then questioned 587 people on October 3 and 4 to test the effect of Blair's speech.
